claim: An IJCNLP 2025 systematic study evaluated 15 LLM judges across roughly 150,000 evaluation instances and found judges systematically favor whichever response occupies a particular slot in the prompt, independent of content quality, with verdicts flipping purely due to response reordering.
stance_target: treating a single-pass LLM-as-judge verdict as a reliable, position-independent quality signal in an adversarial review pipeline
quoted_support: A systematic study at IJCNLP 2025 evaluated 15 LLM judges across roughly 150,000 evaluation instances and found that judges systematically favor whichever response sits in a particular slot of the prompt, and that this effect is not attributable to random chance.

claim: Using a model to judge its own outputs (self-preference bias) inflates the resulting score above what an independent judge from a different model family would assign.
stance_target: using the same model as both generator and adversarial reviewer in the software factory's QC pipeline
quoted_support: Models disproportionately favor outputs generated by themselves or by models in their own family, meaning that if you use GPT-4o to judge GPT-4o's own outputs, the resulting score is inflated above what an independent judge would assign.

claim: The commonly cited statistic that LLM judges reach roughly 80% agreement with human evaluators comes from the original MT-Bench study, describes aggregate benchmark performance, and should not be treated as a production-readiness guarantee for a specific task and judge model.
stance_target: citing the MT-Bench 80% agreement figure as sufficient validation for deploying an LLM judge in a specific production pipeline
quoted_support: The often-cited statistic that LLM judges reach roughly 80% agreement with human evaluators comes from the original MT-Bench study and is accurate as an aggregate figure, but it describes average performance across a broad benchmark — not reliability on your specific task with your specific judge model. Treating that number as a production-readiness guarantee is the mistake.

claim: Position bias can be detected and mitigated with a swap-order audit harness: run the same pairwise comparison twice with response order reversed and measure the verdict-flip rate; mitigation is averaging across orderings or using a judge from a different model family than the one being evaluated.
stance_target: implementing automated bias-detection harnesses as part of the software factory's adversarial review infrastructure
scope_conditions: practical mitigation technique, demonstrated with working Python code
quoted_support: The single highest-leverage check most teams skip: run the same pairwise comparison twice, with the response order swapped, and see whether the verdict flips... Mitigation: average scores across both orderings, or use a separate judge model from a different family than the model being evaluated.

claim: DeepEval is designed to run as a pytest-native CI/CD quality gate (14+ metrics covering hallucination, bias, toxicity, RAG checks) that blocks a merge when a quality-regression test fails, rather than generating a report someone has to remember to read.
stance_target: rigid evals as hard CI blockers rather than advisory reports in a continuously-operating agentic software factory
quoted_support: The pattern that makes DeepEval distinct from a standalone evaluation script is that it runs as a real pytest test, meaning a quality regression fails the build the same way a broken unit test would — instead of generating a report someone has to remember to read.

claim: Promptfoo includes a security-testing suite with 500+ built-in adversarial attack vectors for red-teaming LLM applications.
stance_target: tech stack options for adversarial/red-team testing in the software factory's QC pillar
quoted_support: Promptfoo is CLI-first and YAML-config-driven, strongest at multi-model prompt comparison and adversarial red-teaming, with 500-plus built-in attack vectors in its security-testing suite.

claim: Mature GenAI QA programs typically run two evaluation tools in parallel -- a lightweight CI-blocking framework plus a production-monitoring platform for ongoing drift/regression detection and human review -- rather than relying on a single tool.
stance_target: layered eval/observability architecture combining offline CI gates and online production monitoring for a continuously operating agent fleet
quoted_support: None of these tools wins outright; most mature GenAI QA programs run two of them in parallel: a lightweight framework for blocking bad deploys plus a platform for ongoing monitoring and human review.
